relevance_reason: Reports two new patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome and compound heterozygous RFX6 nonsense mutations, with childhood-onset rather than neonatal diabetes, plus a review of previously reported cases.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported a Turkish girl (case 1) born at 32 weeks' gestation (birth weight 1.65 kg) with duodenal atresia, jejunal web, and Meckel diverticulum, who had hyperglycemia noted at age 2 years and presented at 3 years with diabetic ketoacidosis, very low insulin and C-peptide, and negative islet autoantibodies; she was treated with insulin. She had recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding due to gastric heterotopia in the small bowel, resolved after resection at age 5, and an absent gallbladder with normal liver function. Her identical twin had duodenal atresia and died at 1 month.
quotes: Case 1 (Figure 1, I5), current age 9 years, is a female born at 32 weeks' gestation, birth weight 1.65 kg (42nd centile), with duodenal atresia, jejunal web and Meckel's diverticulum.
She presented at the age of 3 years with diabetic ketoacidosis.
Additional investigation revealed absent gall bladder with otherwise normal biliary tract. Liver function tests have always been within normal limits.

phenotypes.text: gastric heterotopia in small bowel with gastrointestinal bleeding

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported the male double first cousin (case 2) of case 1, born at 34 weeks (birth weight 1.70 kg) with duodenal atresia and midgut malrotation, who had asymptomatic fasting hyperglycemia at age 5 and was diagnosed with diabetes at age 6 years with undetectable insulin, low C-peptide, and negative autoantibodies; he required insulin. He had chronic iron deficiency anemia of unknown cause and no hepatobiliary abnormality. The parents were not consanguineous, but the mothers were sisters and the fathers brothers.
quotes: Case 2 (Figure 1, I12), her double first cousin, current age 9 years, is a male infant who was born at 34 weeks gestation, birth weight 1.70 kg (7th centile), with duodenal atresia and mid-gut malrotation.
He was diagnosed with diabetes having presented with hyperglycemia (16.0 mmol/l) at the age of 6 years.
His past history is notable for chronic iron deficiency anemia.
However, the mothers of the two cases are sisters and the fathers are brothers, making the affected individuals double first cousins.

findings.statement: In 2 Turkish double first cousins with Mitchell-Riley syndrome and childhood-onset diabetes, Sansbury et al. (2015) identified compound heterozygous nonsense mutations in the RFX6 gene, c.2176C>T (p.Arg726X) in exon 17 and c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) in exon 18, by targeted next-generation sequencing confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The fathers were heterozygous for p.Arg726X and the mothers for p.Arg866X; both mutations were inherited from the grandmothers.
quotes: Genetic testing showed that both children are compound heterozygotes for the RFX6 nonsense mutations c.2176C>T (p.Arg726X) and c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) in exons 17 and 18, respectively (Figure 2).
The fathers were heterozygous for p.Arg726X and the mothers heterozygous for p.Arg866X. Further testing demonstrated that the mutations had been inherited from both grandmothers.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) found the RFX6 c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) nonsense mutation in exon 18, in compound heterozygosity with p.Arg726X, in 2 double first cousins with Mitchell-Riley syndrome; it was inherited from the mothers. They predicted that p.Arg866X escapes nonsense-mediated decay because it lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon-exon boundary, producing a partially truncated protein with a preserved DNA-binding domain that might retain some function, whereas p.Arg726X is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: The exon 18 mutation, c.2596C>T (R866X) is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay because it lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon–exon boundary of the gene.
The second mutation, c.2176C>T (R726X), is predicted to be subject to nonsense-mediated decay.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) noted that the 8 previously reported molecularly confirmed cases carried splicing/frameshift mutations in exons 2-8 or missense mutations within or near the DNA-binding domain and had diabetes onset within the first 2 weeks of life, whereas their patients carried the first truncating mutations at the 3-prime end (exons 17 and 18). They suggested that escape of the p.Arg866X allele from nonsense-mediated decay could allow retention of some RFX6 function, resulting in a milder phenotype with later onset of diabetes and absent liver pathology.
quotes: The results of mutation analysis of the eight molecularly confirmed probands (excluding those in the present report) suggest a possible genotype/phenotype correlation.

It is possible that escape from NMD could lead to some retention of function of the RFX6 protein generated from that allele, with a resulting milder phenotype with respect to age of onset of diabetes and other clinical features.

findings.statement: In a review of 8 previously published molecularly confirmed Mitchell-Riley cases, Sansbury et al. (2015) found duodenal atresia in all, with or without jejunal atresia/midgut malrotation, gallbladder agenesis in 7 of 8, intrahepatic cholestasis in 7 of 8 and ascites in another, and death within the first year in 5 of 8. Their 2 new cases differed by childhood-onset diabetes and absence of liver pathology, with longer survival.
quotes: Duodenal atresia is a present in all cases, with or without jejunal atresia/mid-gut malrotation. Gall-bladder agenesis is present in 7/8. All cases had evidence of liver involvement with intrahepatic cholestasis in 7/8 cases and ascites in a further case.
Five of the eight children had died, all within the first year of life.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) found no evidence that heterozygosity for either RFX6 mutation in the family was associated with abnormal HbA1c or C-peptide levels or diabetes, although several heterozygous relatives had adult-onset diabetes; they noted it remained possible that carriers of 5-prime RFX6 mutations might have increased risk of early-onset type 2 diabetes.
quotes: Taking these data together, there is no support for the idea that being heterozygous for either RFX6 mutation is a risk factor for abnormal HbA1c or C-peptide levels, or diabetes.
It remains possible that heterozygous carriers of RFX6 5′ mutations may have increased risk of early-onset type 2 diabetes.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) recommended RFX6 genetic testing in infants with duodenal or jejunal atresia with or without intestinal malrotation even in the absence of neonatal diabetes, especially when sibling recurrence or parental consanguinity suggests autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: Genetic testing for RFX6 mutations should be considered in patients presenting with intestinal atresias in the absence of neonatal diabetes, especially where sibling recurrence or parental consanguinity point to possible autosomal recessive inheritance.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the discovery of RFX6 mutations in infants with autosomal recessive neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresia and gallbladder hypoplasia. It also proposes the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome and describes an Rfx6-null mouse model.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) described human infants with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia. Pancreas size was somewhat reduced, but the patients were not deficient in exocrine pancreatic enzymes. Autopsies of 2 cases showed normal-appearing exocrine pancreata with clusters of chromogranin A-positive cells but no cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin. The syndrome also included a hypoplastic gallbladder and intractable diarrhea that did not respond to pancreatic enzyme replacement.
quotes: The phenotype of the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice is remarkably similar to human patients born with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia.

autopsies of two cases (proband #1 and case 3 in Ref) revealed normal-appearing exocrine pancreata with clusters of ChromograninA-positive cells but total absence of cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin
In addition, the syndrome involves hypoplastic gall bladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement.

phenotypes.text: absence of insulin-, glucagon- and somatostatin-staining cells
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) mapped the disease locus by high-resolution homozygosity mapping in 2 probands, who were the offspring of first-cousin and second-cousin parents, respectively. Only 3 homozygous-by-descent regions were shared by both probands, totaling 24 Mb and containing 194 RefSeq genes. Of these genes, only RFX6, in the largest segment at 6q21-q22, showed pancreas-enriched expression, and its expression in fetal pancreas increased between 10 and 20 weeks.
quotes: The disease locus was mapped using overlapping homozygosity in probands #1and #2 (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports) respectively the offspring of first and second cousins.
Only three HBD regions were common in the two probands, totaling 24 Mb (Table 1). Altogether, 194 RefSeq genes map to these regions.
Of these genes, only RFX6, which falls in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas–enriched expression in the TiGER database

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) used array capture and deep sequencing of exons in the shared homozygous regions in proband 2. Of 30 novel sequence variants detected, the only nonsynonymous one was a ser217-to-pro (S217P) substitution in RFX6. Direct sequencing confirmed this variant in homozygous state in proband 2, the offspring of second cousins, who was alive at age 4.5 years. The variant was inherited from carrier parents. S217P lies between the DNA-binding and dimerization domains; it only modestly reduced DNA binding and did not affect dimer formation.
quotes: The only non-synonymous variant was 217 Ser>Pro in RFX6, identifying this gene as the most likely candidate.
Proband #2, still alive at age 4.5 years, had the homozygous missense mutation 217 Ser>Pro, confirming the unbiased exon sequencing described above.
217S>P (proband #2), which lies between the DNA-binding domain and dimerization domain of Rfx6, only modestly reduced DNA binding (Fig. 5d) and did not affect dimer formation (data not shown).

findings.statement: In proband 1, the offspring of first cousins who died in the first few months of life, Smith et al. (2010) identified a homozygous loss of the RFX6 intron 2 splice donor site (IVS2+2T-C), inherited from carrier parents. RT-PCR of RNA from the proband's autopsy pancreas did not detect the properly spliced transcript. No RNA from exons 1 and 2 was detected either, which the authors attributed probably to nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
we amplified RFX6 mRNA by RT-PCR of high-quality RNA from autopsy pancreas and failed to detect the properly spliced transcript
We also failed to detect any RNA from exons 1+2, upstream of the splicing mutation, probably due to nonsense-mediated decay

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found a homozygous out-of-frame deletion in exon 7 of RFX6 in proband 4, who died in the first few months of life. The mutation was inherited from carrier parents.
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found a homozygous arg181-to-gln (R181Q) missense mutation in RFX6 in proband 5, who died in the first few months of life. The variant was inherited from carrier parents and affects a highly conserved arginine in the DNA-binding domain. In EMSA, R181Q completely abrogated DNA binding.
quotes: the missense mutation 181 R>Q involving a highly conserved arginine in the DNA-binding domain (Supplementary Fig. S15)
We found that 181R>Q (proband #5), which alters a conserved amino acid in the DNA binding domain, completely abrogated DNA binding

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found that proband 3 was compound heterozygous for 2 RFX6 splice mutations: a loss of the intron 6 donor site (IVS6+2T-G) and a disruption of the intron 1 acceptor site (IVS1-12A-G). Both mutations were inherited from carrier parents. This patient was still alive at age 9 years and was intermittently off insulin.
quotes: Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote for donor-site loss in intron 6 (IVS6+2 t>g) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12 a>g).

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found RFX6 mutations in 5 of 6 probands and described a genotype-phenotype correlation. Probands homozygous for a splice-site mutation, a frameshift deletion, or the DNA-binding-abolishing R181Q mutation died in the first few months of life. In contrast, the compound heterozygous proband 3 was alive at age 9 years, and proband 2, homozygous for the modestly hypomorphic S217P, was alive at age 4.5 years.
quotes: Missense, splicing or frameshift mutations in RFX6 were found in five of the six available probands (Fig. 5e) with an interesting genotype-phenotype correlation.
Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life
Proband #2, still alive at age 4.5 years, had the homozygous missense mutation 217 Ser>Pro

phenotypes.text: death in first few months of life

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) described the human syndrome as autosomal recessive. The 2 mapped probands were the offspring of consanguineous parents (first and second cousins), and all identified RFX6 mutations were inherited from carrier parents.
quotes: In human infants with a similar autosomal recessive syndrome of neonatal diabetes, genetic mapping and subsequent sequencing identified mutations in the human RFX6 gene.
All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) did not find an RFX6 mutation in proband 6. Because no DNA from the proband was available, they sequenced both parents and found no point mutation in RFX6 or NEUROG3; long-range PCR detected no RFX6 deletions. The authors considered this case most likely a phenocopy. They also found no RFX6 mutations in a case of Martinez-Frias syndrome.
quotes: Finally, we failed to identify any mutation in RFX6 in proband #6.
In the absence of proband DNA we cannot rule out a de novo mutation, but this case is most likely a phenocopy. We also failed to find RFX6 mutations in a case of the Martinez-Frias syndrome.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) noted that OMIM had listed their cases under Martinez-Frias syndrome. They considered their cases distinct, because the original Martinez-Frias syndrome patients had esophageal atresia and hypospadias and did not have diabetes. They proposed the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome, after the 2 clinicians who first described the condition.
quotes: However, since the original MFS patients also had oesophageal atresia and hypospadias, and did not have diabetes, and we did not find any RFX6 mutation in the parents of one case of MFS, our cases are distinct from MFS.
We propose to name their condition, now of defined molecular aetiology, the Mitchell-Riley syndrome after the two clinicians who first described it.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) generated Rfx6-null mice by replacing the first 5 exons with an eGFP-cre cassette. Homozygous mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio but did not feed normally, had gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction, and died within 2 days of birth; some had reduced pancreas size. At embryonic day 17.5, the mutant pancreata contained many chromogranin A-positive endocrine cells, but none expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin, or ghrelin. Pancreatic polypeptide-expressing cells were increased.
quotes: homozygous Rfx6eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but failed to feed normally, exhibited gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction (Fig. 3e-f) and died within 2 days post partum.
the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre pancreata still contained a large number of endocrine cells, but confirmed that none of these cells expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin or ghrelin (Fig. 4).

findings.statement: In Rfx6-null mouse pancreata, Smith et al. (2010) found that Neurog3 expression was unaffected. Expression of the alpha-cell factors Irx2 and Arx, and of the insulin transcription factors Pax6, MafA, NeuroD1, and Pdx1, was reduced. Nkx2.2 and Nkx6.1 were not significantly changed and Pax4 was increased, and Nkx6.1 expression expanded to all endocrine cells. Primary cilia formation was unaffected, in contrast to Rfx3-null mice.
quotes: The absence of Rfx6 did not affect Neurogenin3 expression, and this was confirmed at the protein level (data not shown).

Interestingly, genes encoding several factors involved in insulin gene transcription (Pax6, MafA, NeuroD1 and Pdx1) also had reduced expression, but some key genes involved in β-cell specification either did not significantly change (Nkx2.2 and Nkx6.1), or increased (Pax4).
Unlike in the Rfx3-/- mice, we found that primary cilia formation was unaffected in the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre islets

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) showed in mice that Rfx6 acts downstream of Neurog3. Rfx6 is expressed broadly in definitive endoderm after gastrulation, becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud, is reactivated by Neurog3 in islet progenitor cells, and is finally restricted to the islets. The authors noted that NEUROG3 mutations also cause intractable diarrhea and diabetes but not small bowel atresia or biliary abnormalities. They attributed this difference to Rfx6 expression in early gut endoderm, where Neurog3 is not expressed.
quotes: Rfx6 is expressed initially broadly in the definitive endoderm after gastrulation, becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud at mid gestation, is reactivated by Neurogenin3 in islet progenitor cells and is ultimately restricted to pancreatic islets in the mature pancreas.

NEUROG3 mutation does not cause the small bowel atresia or biliary abnormalities seen with RFX6 mutation, which is not surprising since Neurogenin3 is not expressed in the early gut endoderm as is Rfx6.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) showed by EMSA that Rfx6 and Rfx3 form a heterodimeric complex that binds an X box site. The 2 factors cooperated in activating a promoter containing multimers of this site. The authors concluded that Rfx3 and Rfx6 cooperate in regulating genes involved in islet development but not in cilia formation.
quotes: We found that both full length Rfx3, and truncations that retain the DNA-binding and dimerization domains, bound to an X box site together with Rfx6 (Fig. 5a and Supplemenatry Fig. S10), and that the two factors cooperated in activating a promoter containing multimers of this X box site (Fig 5b).
We conclude that Rfx3 and Rfx6 cooperate in regulating a set of genes involved in islet development but not in cilia formation.

relevance_reason: This case report describes a newborn of consanguineous parents with Martinez-Frias syndrome (intestinal atresia, gallbladder aplasia, neonatal diabetes, IUGR). That phenotype matches Mitchell-Riley syndrome. The patient also had neonatal hemochromatosis.

findings.statement: Martinovici et al. (2010) reported a newborn of consanguineous parents who had multiple congenital anomalies: intrauterine growth retardation, intestinal atresia, gallbladder aplasia, and diabetes mellitus. The authors made a diagnosis of Martinez-Frias syndrome. The infant also had neonatal hemochromatosis, and the authors suggested that neonatal hemochromatosis may be part of the Martinez-Frias syndrome.
quotes: We report on a newborn from consanguineous parents who presented with multiple congenital anomalies and neonatal hemochromatosis.
The syndrome consisted of intra-uterine growth retardation, intestinal atresia, gallbladder aplasia and diabetes mellitus, and fitted with the diagnosis of Martinez-Frias syndrome
We suggest that neonatal hemochromatosis may be part of the Martinez-Frias syndrome.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Hepatic reticuloendothelial system cell iron deposition

findings.statement: Martinovici et al. (2010) described Martinez-Frias syndrome as a very rare autosomal recessive phenotype whose gene had not yet been identified. Their patient was born to consanguineous parents.
quotes: fitted with the diagnosis of Martinez-Frias syndrome, a very rare autosomal recessive phenotype, the gene of which remains to be identified
We report on a newborn from consanguineous parents

relevance_reason: This paper describes TiGER, a bioinformatics database of tissue-specific gene expression and regulation. It never mentions Mitchell-Riley syndrome, RFX6, neonatal diabetes, pancreatic hypoplasia, intestinal atresia, or gallbladder abnormalities, and it reports no patients, variants or disease-relevant experiments.
Case report of a patient with neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gallbladder agenesis (the Mitchell-Riley phenotype), with discussion of inheritance and exclusion of candidate genes.

findings.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) reported a patient born to consanguineous parents who had neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias, and gallbladder agenesis. This was the first such case with neonatal diabetes and no demonstrable structural abnormality of the pancreas, which the authors said showed that a deficit in pancreatic function is involved.
quotes: We report a patient born to consanguineous parents as a further example of a recently described phenotype comprising neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gall bladder agenesis.
Our case is the first to have neonatal diabetes without a demonstrable structural pancreatic abnormality, showing that a deficit in pancreatic function is involved.

findings.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) noted that other reported cases had overlapping patterns, including malrotation, biliary atresia, and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g., as described by Martinez-Frias), and proposed that these cases may be variations of the same syndrome.
quotes: Other reports have described cases with overlapping patterns including malrotation, biliary atresia and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g. as described by Martínez-Frías). We propose that these cases may represent variations of the same syndrome.

findings.statement: Because their patient was born to consanguineous parents, Chappell et al. (2008) concluded that the disorder is likely inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: It is likely that this disorder is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

findings.statement: In their patient, Chappell et al. (2008) sequenced genes known to cause monogenic diabetes (KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1-beta, NeuroD1, and TCF7L2) and the candidate gene HNF6, which is involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development. They found no mutations.
quotes: We sequenced genes with a recognized role in monogenic forms of diabetes, including KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1beta, NeuroD1 and TCF7L2, as well as a novel candidate gene, HNF6, known to be involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development, but did not identify mutations.

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation (Martinez-Frias syndrome), which is part of the Mitchell-Riley syndrome spectrum.

findings.statement: Galán-Gómez et al. (2007) described a female infant born to consanguineous parents who had a multiple congenital anomaly pattern of low birth weight, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation. She died 60 days after birth. High-resolution chromosome analysis (550-600 bands) was normal (46,XX).
quotes: We describe a patient born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern characterized by low birth weight, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation.
The infant died 60 days after birth. Chromosomes at 550-600 band levels were normal for a female (46,XX).

findings.statement: Galán-Gómez et al. (2007) concluded that their patient, born to consanguineous parents, confirmed the autosomal recessive disorder previously described by their group (Martínez-Frías syndrome).
quotes: This patient confirmed the autosomal recessive disorder previously described by our group.

findings.statement: Galán-Gómez et al. (2007) suggested that the pathogenesis of the syndrome is most probably of blastogenetic origin, mainly affecting the midline developmental duodenal-biliary-pancreatic junction.
quotes: The pathogenesis of this syndrome is most probably of blastogenetic origin mainly affecting midline developmental duodenal biliary pancreatic junction.

relevance_reason: This paper first described the syndrome of neonatal diabetes with pancreatic hypoplasia, intestinal atresia and gallbladder hypoplasia, which the entry is named after.

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants (2 sibling pairs from 2 families and 1 isolated case) with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia, and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder. One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents. Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management, and 1 patient with a milder form was surviving without insulin.
quotes: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia.
One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents. One patient with a milder form is surviving free of insulin. Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management.

phenotypes.text: death in first year of life

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) performed pancreatic immunohistochemistry in 3 of the infants. It showed a few scattered chromogranin A-positive cell clusters but no insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin staining at all. Exocrine histology varied between cases.
quotes: Immunohistochemical staining for pancreatic islet hormones was performed on three of the infants.
Pancreatic immunohistochemistry revealed few scattered chromogranin-A-positive cell clusters but complete absence of insulin, glucagon and somatostatin. Exocrine histology was variable.

phenotypes.text: absence of pancreatic islet hormone-producing cells
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) concluded that the condition probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome. Their evidence was the affected sibling pairs, one of which was born to consanguineous parents.
quotes: This combination of multiple congenital abnormalities has not been previously described and probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development

findings.statement: In 1 patient from the consanguineous family, Mitchell et al. (2004) found no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL1 at 6q24 and no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene. They also found no mutation in the coding sequences or splice sites of PDX1.
quotes: In one case from the consanguineous family, molecular analysis showed no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL-1 at 6q24, no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene, and no mutation in the coding sequences or splice sites of PDX-1.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a patient with intestinal and biliary atresias, intestinal malrotation, a malformed or hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias, and presents this as further evidence of a distinct syndrome. These features overlap with Mitchell-Riley syndrome.

findings.statement: Gentile and Fiorente (1999) reported a case with esophageal, duodenal, rectoanal and biliary atresia, intestinal malrotation, a malformed/hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias. They considered this further evidence of a new distinct syndrome.
quotes: Esophageal, duodenal, rectoanal and biliary atresia, intestinal malrotation, malformed/hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias: further evidence of a new distinct syndrome.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a lethal autosomal recessive syndrome with intrauterine growth retardation, biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia, which overlaps the intestinal atresia and hepatobiliary features of Mitchell-Riley syndrome.

findings.statement: Annerén et al. (1998) described a lethal syndrome with intrauterine growth retardation, intra- and extrahepatic biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia. They considered it to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: Lethal autosomal recessive syndrome with intrauterine growth retardation, intra- and extrahepatic biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia.

relevance_reason: The paper describes 2 sibs born to consanguineous parents who had duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia and a hypoplastic pancreas. This overlaps with the Mitchell-Riley phenotype and suggests autosomal recessive inheritance.

findings.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) described 2 sibs born to consanguineous parents who had a multiple congenital anomaly pattern. It included low birth weight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and hypospadias.
quotes: We studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern which includes low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias.

findings.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) concluded that the constellation of anomalies in sibs born to consanguineous parents appeared to represent a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.
quotes: This constellation of congenital anomalies appears to be a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.

findings.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) searched the data files of the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC). They found 3 other unrelated infants with intestinal atresias, hypospadias and low birth weight, and suggested these cases may represent a milder expression of the same syndrome.
quotes: A computerized search of the data files of the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC) identified 3 other unrelated infants with intestinal atresias, hypospadias, and low birth weight.
These cases may represent a milder expression of the same syndrome.
